clue.text: Call for the final delivery

explanation.surface: A request for the last round of the postman's day.
explanation.walkthrough: The Last Post is the bugle call sounded at military funerals and at close of day; read literally it is the final post of the day.
explanation.definitionFit: A bugle call played at funerals and remembrance services, and also literally the day's closing round of mail.

clue.text: In tax, it suggests thoughtlessness

indicators.note: it is put in the word for tax

parts.note: a levy is a tax

explanation.surface: Within taxation, the word suggests a careless attitude.
explanation.definitionFit: Lack of seriousness, frivolity or flippancy.

clue.text: Make fun of the second to finish

parts.note: to end up is to finish

explanation.surface: Mocking whoever came second in the race.
explanation.definitionFit: To parody or satirise someone.

clue.text: Not quite jiggery but allied to pokery?

definitions.text: Not quite jiggery but allied to pokery?

parts.words: Not quite jiggery but allied to pokery?
parts.note: a word one letter off jiggery, and linked to pokery as a pig is to a poke, as in buying a pig in a poke

explanation.surface: Something almost jiggery that goes with pokery, as in the phrase jiggery-pokery.
explanation.walkthrough: Change the J of jiggery to P; 'pokery' recalls a pig in a poke (a bag), so a place of pigs.
explanation.definitionFit: A pigsty or pig farm, where swine are kept.

clue.text: Southern refuge — an island

parts.note: Noah's ark was a refuge

explanation.surface: A southern haven that is an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Sark is one of the Channel Islands, between England and France.
explanation.definitionFit: A small Channel Island near Guernsey.

clue.text: Cork? Don't retire here

explanation.surface: Someone asked whether to plug a bottle is told to stay out of bed in this spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retire' here means go to bed, so not retiring is staying awake late; 'here' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To cork is to plug or seal a hole, and staying out of bed late is the other sense of the phrasal verb.

clue.text: Sailor wearing a president's cap

parts.note: a tar is a sailor
Bush is the name of two American presidents

explanation.surface: A seaman wearing headgear belonging to a president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' is a link here; the pieces stand side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A tasselled brimless hat like a fez, worn in the Middle East.

clue.text: Drawn-out epic that is really pitiful

indicators.note: drawn out of shape, so these letters are pulled into a new order

explanation.surface: A long epic poem that is truly dreadful.
explanation.definitionFit: Miserably inadequate, arousing pity or contempt.

clue.text: Drill to force open, indeed?

indicators.note: read indeed as in deed: the deed goes in the word for force open

parts.note: to prise is to lever or force open
an act is a deed

explanation.surface: A drill used to lever something open, indeed.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'indeed' as 'in deed': ACT goes inside PRISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To train by repeated exercises, rehearse.

clue.text: Peevish, finding cigarette end in gravy that's lumpy

indicators.note: gravy that is lumpy is badly mixed, so these letters are mixed up too
the end of the word cigarette is its final letter, taken alone here

explanation.surface: A grumpy diner finds a cigarette butt in lumpy gravy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's lumpy' rearranges E (the end of 'cigarette'), IN and GRAVY into the answer; 'in' is fodder, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sour like the condiment, figuratively bad-tempered and irritable.

clue.text: In favour of a drink — shrub!

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
tea is a drink

explanation.surface: A toast proposed in favour of having a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A South African flowering bush with large showy blooms.

clue.text: Thus be flushed but no longer excited

parts.note: so means thus
taken as written
red means flushed in the face

explanation.surface: Someone flushed with excitement calms down.
explanation.definitionFit: Calmed down, made serious or quiet.

clue.text: Socially acceptable in top quarters to sport one?

indicators.note: the letter for socially acceptable goes inside the word top

parts.note: taken as written
U is the old label for upper-class, socially acceptable usage
E and E: compass points are quarters, and east is E

explanation.surface: A question of whether it is acceptable in high society to wear something.
explanation.walkthrough: U (upper-class, acceptable) sits inside TOP, then two compass quarters EE follow. 'One' stands for the thing being sported on top.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairpiece is the item a balding man might sport on top of his head.

clue.text: Will, for example, party cut housing employees?

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: the word cut holds the employees inside it

parts.note: taken as written
men are workers, employees

explanation.surface: A will drafted to trim staff numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'housing' puts MEN inside CUT to make CUMENT, after DO (party).
explanation.definitionFit: A will is one kind of legal paper, a written record of someone's wishes.

clue.text: Waves through formal proposals

explanation.surface: Points made through formal proposals.
explanation.walkthrough: Someone who motions a car through waves it on; motions are also proposals put to a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Gestures someone on with the hand, and proposals put to a vote at a meeting.

clue.text: Form of light entertainment in which some bright sparks shone

definitions.text: Form of light entertainment in which some bright sparks shone

parts.words: Form of light entertainment in which some bright sparks shone
parts.note: light entertainment sounds like comedy on TV with clever performers, but the light and sparks are literal: a fireworks display

explanation.surface: A TV variety show where clever people shone.
explanation.definitionFit: A fireworks display is entertainment made of light, full of real sparks.

clue.text: Adverse reaction to brief experience of the underworld

parts.note: Dis is the Roman underworld, or its god
a taste is a brief experience of something

explanation.surface: Disliking a short visit to the land of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: A feeling of dislike or aversion.

clue.text: Play the banjo to favourite, but promiscuous, lady

parts.note: to strum is to play a stringed instrument like a banjo
a pet is a favourite

explanation.surface: Playing the banjo to a promiscuous woman.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a woman of loose morals, a prostitute.

clue.text: Ken let nice Nigel off

indicators.note: off means bad or gone wrong, so these letters are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: Ken allowed nice Nigel to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ken' looks like a man's name beside Nigel, but it is the definition: ken means knowledge. 'off' rearranges LET NICE NIGEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Ken is one's range of knowledge or understanding, a sense of brains and information.

clue.text: Military unit, on capturing rebel leader shows restraint

indicators.note: the military unit holds the rebel's first letter inside it

parts.note: a legion is a large army unit

indicators.note: the leader of rebel is its first letter

explanation.surface: An army unit captures a rebel chief and holds them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on capturing' (upon capturing) puts R, from 'leader' of 'rebel', into LEGION.
explanation.definitionFit: A shackle fitted round the ankle, used to restrain prisoners.

clue.text: Emotion cunningly concealed by companion, with a smile?

parts.note: CH is short for Companion of Honour
a grin is a smile

explanation.surface: A feeling hidden by a friend who just smiles.
explanation.definitionFit: Annoyance or mortification, often hidden behind a forced smile.

clue.text: Salt offered to the Italian god

parts.note: al is Italian for to the
Kali is a Hindu deity

explanation.surface: Salt offered as a sacrifice to an Italian god.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry, a base that neutralises acids; salts were the early sense.

clue.text: Swine, it's said, abandoning river to web-footed creatures

indicators.note: the river letter is left out of the word for swine

parts.note: rotters are swine, bad people

explanation.surface: Pigs, people say, leaving a river to the water animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's said' flags that swine means rotters in the colloquial sense, not pigs.
explanation.definitionFit: River mammals with webbed feet.

clue.text: Can force to contain drug abuse be on the march?

indicators.note: the can and force letters hold the scrambled drug inside them

parts.note: a tin is a can
G is the symbol for gravitational force

indicators.note: abuse of the word drug misuses its letters, rearranging them

explanation.surface: Can a police force tackle drug abuse while marching?
explanation.walkthrough: 'abuse' turns DRUG into RUDG, which 'to contain' puts inside TIN + G.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking slowly and heavily, plodding as on a long march.

clue.text: Secret vote bringing tax rebate to graduate

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

indicators.note: read as re-bate, the tax is sent back, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: a toll is a tax or charge

explanation.surface: A secret vote on giving a tax refund to a graduate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebate' turns TOLL round to LLOT, placed after BA.
explanation.definitionFit: Voting by paper slips cast in private.

clue.text: First mate right, as always

parts.note: Eve was Adam's mate, the first woman

explanation.surface: The first mate on a ship is right, as always.
explanation.definitionFit: At all times, forever.

clue.text: Choice foreign national upheld

indicators.note: read upheld as up held, the up being held inside the national

parts.note: a Serb is a national of Serbia
taken as written

explanation.surface: A selection of foreign citizen is supported.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'upheld' as UP held: UP is held inside SERB.
explanation.definitionFit: Choice as an adjective means excellent, top-quality.

clue.text: Defeated, arrived by air

parts.note: over, flying over, travelling overhead through the air
came means arrived

explanation.surface: Someone who lost a contest flew in.
explanation.definitionFit: Got the better of an opponent, beat.

clue.text: Carry on, using former nurse

parts.note: ex means former
to tend is to nurse

explanation.surface: Continuing to use an ex-nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: To prolong or continue something further.

clue.text: Drinks and cheese being brought around

indicators.note: the cheese phrase is brought round the word and, enclosing it

parts.note: brie's, read as brie is: brie is a cheese and being is is
taken as written

explanation.surface: Drinks and a cheese board are being carried round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought around' puts AND inside BRIE'S, read as BRIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirits distilled from wine, such as cognac.
